name: Vast Desert
description: A parched expanse of sandy dunes, desolate salt flats, and windblown rock formations.

features.name: Endless Sands
features.description: Countdown (8). To cross the desert, the party must complete the countdown. It ticks down whenever a PC succeeds on an action roll to navigate the seemingly endless expanse.
features.prompt: How do the PCs travel through the desert? What beyond the extreme distance and lack of water makes this area difficult to cross?

features.name: Water Supply
features.prompt: When the party starts their journey, place a number of tokens on this stat block equal to 1 + the number of PCs in the scene. Remove a token at the end of each long rest or when a PC fails an action roll to navigate the desert. When a token would be removed but there are none left, each PC must mark a HP and a Stress. A PC can add a token to this stat block by using a downtime move and making a successful Knowledge Roll to hunt for water. What sorts of water-preserving flora or terrain features have the PCs heard might be found in this desert? How do the PCs collect and carry the water they find?

features.name: Shifting Sands
features.description: The ever-shifting dunes and the whipping wind make trailing creatures through this environment difficult. Action rolls to track creatures through the desert are made with disadvantage.
features.prompt: How do the dunes and landscape shift whenever the heroes rest? What is covered or uncovered by the wind?

features.name: Thunderstorm
features.description: Spend a Fear to have a torrential downpour soak the land. Each PC must either seek shelter from the storm or collect rainwater. Each PC who seeks shelter marks a Stress. The PCs who collect rainwater make a group action roll. • On a success with Hope, add 1d4 tokens to the Water Supply. • On a success with Fear, add 1 token to the Water Supply. • On a failure with Hope, each PC who took part in the group action roll marks a Stress. • On a failure with Fear, each PC who took part in the group action roll marks a Stress, and the PC who rolled the lowest takes 2d8+4 physical damage from the storm.
features.prompt: How does the storm look to the heroes as it rolls in from miles away? Is the storm natural or unnatural? How can you tell?

features.name: Sandstorm
features.description: Spend a Fear to summon a sandstorm that disorients and harries travelers. Each PC takes 2d6+3 physical damage. Until the sandstorm dissipates, a PC who makes an action roll must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll to avoid the swirl of rocks and debris or take 2d6+3 physical damage.
features.prompt: What do the dwellers of this desert wear to weather the sandstorms? How are the dwelling places the party finds here designed to withstand the winds? WITCH’S HUT
